Spark Technologies has reviewed all four capability requirements submitted by ADICC. Our assessment
evaluated each requirement against three criteria: technical feasibility, UAE construction context fit, and
alignment with ADICC's existing systems and workflows.
ADICC currently evaluates Togal.AI as a benchmark for AI-powered estimation. Togal.AI uses deep
learning to analyse PDF drawings and automatically generate quantity takeoffs with team collaboration on a
single project. While effective in its current form, it does not natively support UAE trade rate structures,
authority submission formats, or Arabic-language drawing sets.
Our proposed solution is a custom-built AI Estimation Engine that ingests PDF and CAD drawing sets,
automatically detects and classifies building elements by type, and generates itemised quantity takeoffs
mapped to ADICC's preferred cost database and UAE trade rates. The system supports full team
collaboration, version comparison across drawing revisions, and direct export to ADICC's estimating and
ERP workflows. The AI is trained on drawing conventions common across UAE projects, including
authority-standard drawing formats and Arabic-language annotation.
ADICC currently evaluates nPlan as a benchmark for schedule risk analytics. nPlan integrates with
Primavera P6 and automates Quantitative Schedule Risk Analysis using machine learning trained on
historical schedule data. The core gap for ADICC is the absence of UAE-specific project data in existing
platforms and the lack of native alignment with ADICC's specific P6 environment and reporting workflows.
Our proposed solution is a custom AI Schedule Risk platform that connects directly to ADICC's existing
Primavera P6 environment via native XER/XML export — no schedule rebuild required. The platform runs
automated QSRA using a risk model trained on historical construction schedule data from the UAE and
GCC region, identifies at-risk milestones, flags logic issues, and generates early-warning reports in formats
aligned to ADICC's project controls standards. A natural language agent allows planners and project
managers to interrogate schedule risk in plain English.
ADICC currently evaluates Masin.AI as a benchmark for contract and claims management. Masin.AI
reviews contracts clause by clause, flags risks, drafts claims, calculates entitlements, and prepares
arbitration pleadings, trained on real arbitration cases across FIDIC and GCC construction disputes.
Our proposed solution is a custom AI Contract Intelligence platform trained specifically on ADICC's own
contract portfolio, UAE construction law, FIDIC Red/Yellow/Silver Book standards, DIAC and ADCCAC
arbitration precedents, and GCC-specific claims protocols. The platform reviews new contracts clause by
clause against a risk library built from ADICC's historical claims experience, drafts notices and extension of
time submissions, calculates financial entitlements, and prepares structured arbitration pleadings with
evidence organisation. It is designed to operate from the contract seeding stage onward as a prevention
tool, not just a reactive claims instrument.
ADICC requires a tool enabling stakeholders to access internal company documents through natural
language queries. The original requirement specified WhatsApp as the interface. However, WhatsApp's
Business API imposes restrictions that make it unsuitable for this use case: a mandatory 24-hour
messaging window, strict Meta-approved message template requirements, severe limitations on automated
bot responses, and no support for file retrieval within automated flows.
We recommend Telegram as the interface for this module. Telegram's fully open Bot API supports unlimited
automated messaging, file delivery, natural language query handling, and role-based access controls with
no platform restrictions on automation. The Telegram bot connects to ADICC's internal document repository
via a Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline — users send natural language queries, the system
searches the document library using vector-based semantic search, and returns accurate, source-cited
responses within seconds. Integration with ADICC's existing file repository is included in scope.

The AI processing pipeline is built around a shared platform foundation with four module-specific
processing tracks. The shared foundation — ingestion framework, application logic, unified dashboard, and
ADICC systems integration — is deployed once and shared across all modules.
Module 1 Pipeline — AI Estimation & Quantity Takeoff
Step 1 — Drawing ingestion pipeline accepts PDF, DWG, and scanned drawing sets. OCR and layout
analysis extract text, dimensions, and spatial relationships from each page.
Step 2 — Page classification model identifies drawing type (floor plan, elevation, section, structural, MEP)
and routes to the appropriate detection model.
Step 3 — YOLOv10-based element detection model identifies and classifies all building elements per
drawing page with bounding boxes, labels, and confidence scores.
Step 4 — Quantity calculation engine computes net and gross quantities per element type, applying
UAE-standard waste factors, coverage rates, and measurement rules.
Step 5 — Cost mapping engine assigns unit rates from ADICC's rate database and UAE market rates to
produce preliminary cost estimates per element and per trade.
Step 6 — Output layer generates itemised BOQ, drawing markup, and cost plan. Data pushed to ERP.
Version delta report generated if a previous drawing revision exists.
Module 2 Pipeline — AI Schedule Risk & Project Controls
Step 1 — P6 XER/XML export ingested. Schedule parsed into activity network with logic relationships,
Step 2 — Schedule integrity engine runs automated DCMA 14-point check plus AI-identified logic issues,
open ends, and constraint density analysis.
Step 3 — AI risk model assigns duration uncertainty distributions to every activity based on activity type,
sector, and GCC historical schedule performance data.
Step 4 — Monte Carlo simulation runs probabilistic forecast for every milestone. P50, P70, and P80
completion dates calculated with confidence intervals.
Step 5 — Driving path analysis identifies activities most influential on each key milestone. Risk ranking
Step 6 — Dashboard and reports published. Milestone alert engine monitors subsequent schedule updates
and triggers notifications when risk thresholds are breached.
Module 3 Pipeline — AI Contract Management & Claims
Step 1 — Contract document ingested and parsed at clause level. FIDIC book type, bespoke amendments,
and UAE-specific provisions identified and tagged.
Step 2 — Clause risk engine reviews every clause against ADICC's risk library, UAE law requirements, and
FIDIC standard provisions. Risk score assigned per clause.
Step 3 — Risk alert engine monitors project event feed (delays, instructions, variations) and maps events to
contract clause obligations, triggering notice drafting.
Step 4 — Notice and claims drafting engine auto-generates contractual notices, EoT submissions, and
claims narratives. Entitlement calculation engine runs financial quantum.
Step 5 — Arbitration preparation module assembles structured pleading with legal arguments, evidence
index, case law citations, and cross-examination questions.
Step 6 — All contract actions, notices, and claims logged to audit trail. Document version history
maintained. Reports generated for commercial management review.
Module 4 Pipeline — Telegram Document Access Bot
Step 1 — Document indexing pipeline connects to ADICC's file repository via SharePoint/OneDrive API or
network drive connector. All supported document types ingested and chunked.
Step 2 — Sentence transformer model converts document chunks into dense vector embeddings stored in
the Qdrant vector database with metadata tags.
Step 3 — User sends natural language query via Telegram. Bot receives the query via webhook and
passes it to the RAG query engine.
Step 4 — Query embedded using the same sentence transformer. Qdrant performs semantic search across
document embeddings. Top-K relevant chunks retrieved.
Step 5 — Retrieved chunks passed as context to the LLM alongside the user query. LLM generates a
grounded, accurate answer citing source documents.
Step 6 — Answer and source citations delivered to the user in Telegram. Query and response logged to
audit trail with user identity and timestamp.
